questions.q: Why couldn't Foundations' plain Parquet material safely do a row-level UPDATE or DELETE?
options: A Parquet folder isn't built for safe in-place row changes — there's no transaction log to make it atomic
PySpark has no concept of filtering or removing rows at all
UPDATE and DELETE are only valid in Pandas, never in Spark
Parquet files cannot store numeric columns
questions.explain: Delta can do this because UPDATE/DELETE are just more commits, using the same log mechanism from Lesson 17.

questions.q: What does MERGE INTO do that separate UPDATE and INSERT statements can't do as cleanly?
options: Updates matching rows and inserts new ones in a single atomic statement, without needing to find matches yourself first
It only performs deletes, never updates or inserts
It requires converting the table back to plain Parquet first
It has no real advantage over separate statements
questions.explain: WHEN MATCHED updates the existing row; WHEN NOT MATCHED inserts the new one — both handled atomically.

questions.q: What real-world problem is the "upsert" pattern built for?
options: A daily file of records where some rows are corrections to existing data and some are brand new
Deleting an entire table in one operation
Converting CSV files to Parquet
Aggregating data across multiple partitions
questions.explain: This is exactly the mechanism this course's Chapter 3 relies on for building a silver layer from bronze.

questions.q: Where does the DataFrame-API version of MERGE come from?
options: The delta.tables module, providing a DeltaTable object these Delta-specific operations are called on
It's part of pyspark.sql, the same module used throughout Foundations
It requires installing pandas separately
It's only available through the SQL syntax, never the DataFrame API
questions.explain: This is genuinely new material — Foundations' PySpark never wrote to a Delta table at all.

questions.q: How do UPDATE and DELETE actually get recorded in the transaction log?
options: As more commits — new files with the changed/remaining rows, plus remove actions for the old ones
They bypass the transaction log entirely and modify files directly in place
They require a completely separate log format from regular writes
UPDATE and DELETE don't generate any log entries at all
questions.explain: This is the exact add/remove mechanism from Lesson 17, now doing real work for row-level changes.
